items.text: Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York
National Portrait Gallery, London (his portrait by George Richmond, 1829)
Met William Blake through John Linnell; Blake's influence shapes the next ten years of work
Lived at Shoreham, Kent ('Rat Abbey', then Water House); visionary pastoral landscapes; centre of the Blake-inspired group the Ancients (with George Richmond and Edward Calvert)
Returned to London, settling in Marylebone; later worked for two decades as a private drawing master
Married Hannah Linnell; two-year honeymoon in Italy
Full member of the (Old) Water Colour Society
Moved to Furze Hill House, Redhill, Surrey
Late watercolours illustrating Milton's L'Allegro and Il Penseroso; etchings illustrating Virgil
Honorary Fellow of the Society of Painter-Etchers (Hon. RE)
Died at Redhill; buried at St Mary's, Reigate
